chunks: There is a mosque at my door in which there are people who oppose and are hostile. They remain in prayer in the evening, and I pray the Asr prayer, then go out and pray with them.
So he said: "Would you not be pleased that it be counted for you as twenty-four prayers?"

key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: the prayer, here referring to ritual salat
key_terms.تُحْسَبَ: to be counted or reckoned as reward
key_terms.مَسْجِدًا: a mosque, the place of congregational prayer
key_terms.مُخَالِفُونَ: those who differ in religious affiliation or position
key_terms.مُعَانِدُونَ: those who are hostile or obstinate

ai.seo_question: Is there reward in repeating a prayer with others in congregation after already praying it?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses praying with a group identified as opponents, after one has already performed the Asr prayer individually. The Imam عليه السلام indicates the merit and reward of joining them in congregational prayer, such that it is counted with multiplied reward.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1212 - He also said to Imam (as):
"There is a mosque near my door in which there are people who oppose and are hostile. They remain in prayer during the evening, and I pray Asr and then go out and join them in prayer."
Imam (as) said: "Would you not be pleased to have it counted for you as twenty-four prayers?".
